overview:
# Circuit Element Editor Overview
*Double click on an element to open the Circuit Element Navigator.*

*Click the Editor button to open the Circuit Element Editor.*

The program uses a circuit element modeling method to simulate the electrical power delivery and distribution system. Electrical circuit components are represented by circuit elements that provide the appropriate mathematical model for accurately modeling a circuit. Circuit elements can be edited using the Circuit Element Navigator and Circuit Element Editor. 

The Circuit Element Editor is an extension of the Circuit Element Navigator. While the Navigator provides a way for you to edit the data fields common to all circuit element types and to navigate through your model, the Editor allows you to access and modify all data for the currently selected element. 

The Circuit Element Editor overview 

## 1—Circuit Element Navigator: 
The window from which the Circuit Element Editor can be opened. The Circuit Element Navigator provides a way for you to edit the data fields common to all circuit element types and to navigate through your model. 

## 2—Tabs: 
The tabs present on the Circuit Element Editor will depend on the element you have selected and the functionalities you have available in your program. See the list below for pages on specific Circuit Element Editor tabs. Also see the All Tabs section for a complete list of all the available tabs. 

- Arc Flash Tab
- Billing Load Tab
- Calculated Load Tab
- Capacitor Data Tab
- Conductor Data Tab
- Consumer Data Tab
- Consumer Generation Tab
- Device Data Tab
- External Tab
- Fault Model Tab
- Files Tab
- Generator Data Tab
- Impedance Tab
- Load Settings Tab
- Locked Rotor Tab
- Motor Data Tab
- Node Data Tab
- Polygons Tab
- Profiles Tab
- Regulator Data Tab
- Reliability Tab
- Soft Start Tab
- Solar Generator Output Tab
- Solar Array Tab
- Solar Fault Model Tab
- Solar Inverter Tab
- Source Data Tab
- Switch Data Tab
- Switching Options Tab
- Transformer Data Tab 

*Note: solar PV element tabs will be disabled unless the solar PV feature license is validated on application start*

*Tip: This tab is related to the overhead and underground lines. Other data tabs will appear in the Circuit Element Editor based on what element you have selected. Click on the link to read about the “Conductor Data” tab and to view the links to the other data tabs.* 

## 3—Equipment Editor Button: 
Brings up the Equipment Editor, which allows you to assign hardware assets to various parts of the currently selected element. The names of any assigned equipment will appear in the text box to the left of this button. See the Equipment Editor section for more information on the Equipment Editor. 

## 4—Assets Button: 
Brings up the Asset Selector. 

## 5—Status Bar: 
The Circuit Element Navigator side of the status bar displays the source and feeder, respectively, which are connected to the currently active element. The Circuit Element Editor side of the status bar displays the voltage, line connection type, and load connection type of the currently active element.
general:
# About Circuit Elements and Connectivity

The WindMil model is composed of many discrete parts called circuit elements. These elements represent parts of your real-world system, such as substations, switches, and lines. 

WindMil allows 15 types of circuit elements, as shown in the Circuit Element Symbols table. 

| Symbol Element Type | Symbol Element Type |
| --- | --- | 
| Source | Overcurrent Device |
| Overhead | Node |
| Underground | Generator |
| Regulator | Motor |
| Transformer | Switchgear |
| Switch | Consumer |
| Capacitor | Map Point |
| Solar Photo-Voltaic Generator ||

Some of these element types can actually represent multiple real-world elements. The overcurrent device is a workhorse element; it can represent a fuse, circuit breaker, sectionalizer, or any other overcurrent device. The consumer element can represent residential consumers, small commercial consumers, large commercial consumers, motor loads, irrigation, oil and gas companies, or test meters. The map point can represent poles, traffic lights, pull boxes, vaults, markers, or foreign structures. 

If you’re not sure about the type of an element, simply place the editing cursor over the element. You can then look at the status bar, which will display the name, element type, and phase of the element you have chosen to hover over. 

## Parent-Child Connectivity

Circuit elements are not just drawn on the screen. They store information about the hardware they represent in the real world, including its location and its relationship to the rest of the circuit. These relationships, taken together, make up the circuit’s connectivity. 

The connectivity of a circuit will always tell you the direction of electrical flow. Generally, flow begins at a source and proceeds downline, branching outward like the delta of a big river. Every element knows about the element immediately upline (called its parent) and any elements immediately downline (called its children).This is called parent-child connectivity. 

Parent Child Connectivity Example 


```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Start((Source #1))---OH1(OH #1)
  OH1---OH4(OH #4)
  OH1---OH9(OH #9)
  OH1---UG1(UG #1)
```

In the image above, Source #1 has no parent and its only child is OH #1. OH #1 has Source #1 as its parent and three children named OH #4, OH #9, and UG 1, which have OH #1 as their parent. 

Source elements never have a parent, as there can never be anything upline from the circuit’s source of power. However, sometimes other elements will be left without a parent. These elements are called disconnected elements and, by default, they will draw pink in most view modes. 

When you are editing a model, you should always pay careful attention to these parent-child relationships. When you are looking at many elements that are very close together, it may be difficult to know which element is the parent and which is the child. One way to be sure that you are interpreting the model view correctly is to use the Trace Circuit view mode option.
arc_flash:
## Arc Flash Calculation Method 
This allows you to specify the calculation standard to be applied to the selected elements. At present, the available options are “IEEE 1584-2018”, “NESC”, and “None”, which will cause these elements to be skipped when running analysis. 

## Electrode Configuration 
The configuration of electrodes to use when calculating arc flash energy. Please refer to IEEE 1584-2018 for an explanation of the available options. 

## Gap between electrodes 
The arc gap between electrodes. 

## Working Distance to Arc 
The distance from element's electrodes (point of arc) to the working person's torso. 

## Width of Enclosure 
The physical width of the element's enclosure, if any. Elements in open air (specified as electrode configurations VOA or HOA) do not use this value. 

## Height of Enclosure 
The physical height of the element's enclosure, if any. Elements in open air (specified as electrode configurations VOA or HOA) do not use this value. 

## Depth of Enclosure 
The physical depth of the element's enclosure, if any. Elements in open air (specified as electrode configurations VOA or HOA) do not use this value. 

The “Arc Flash” tab in the Circuit Element Editor 

## Arc Type 
When the “NESC” calculation method is selected, this section allows you to set the arc type for each element in the selection set based on the phase count. At present, the available options are “1-Phase Open-Air”, “1-Phase Enclosure”, “3-Phase Open-Air”, and “3-Phase Enclosure”.
billing_load:
Billing Load is the kW, kvar, kWh, Consumer, and kVA load data assigned to each phase of overhead, underground, and node type circuit elements. This is used by the Load Allocation analysis to generate kW and kvar calculated load. 

## Load Group List 
The box at the top of this tab, which contains the load groups you have assigned for accumulating loading information. To create additional groups, edit your Load Allocation Preferences. 

## Billing Load Data Table 
The table at the bottom of the tab. The column headers in this table contain each existing phase that is defined for the load group. The row headers contain certain load groups, defined below. Each phase record contains the amount of billing load assigned to a load group. There can be up to five load groups, each with three phases, so a total of fifteen records could exist. 

## Group Column 
Contains the load groups of the table. 

## kW 
Metered kW demand. 

## kvar 
Metered kvar demand. 

## kWh 
The kilowatt hour usage. 

## Consumer 
The number of consumers. 

## kVA 
The connected transformer kVA.
calculated_load:
Calculated Load is the kW and kvar assigned to each phase of overhead, underground, and node type circuit elements. Calculated Load is used by analysis algorithms to calculate current (load) flow, and this tab is the same for all overhead, underground, consumer, and node-type circuit elements. 

## When kW is Changed Hold 
Recalculates values in the Calculated Load Table when kW is changed. Power Factor recalculates the kvar based upon the currently-displayed %PF value. The %PF value will not be changed. kVAR recalculates the %PF based upon the currently-displayed kvar value. The kvar value will not be changed. 

## Enter Load Using 
Activates certain fields in the Calculated Load Table. kW, kvar and PF activates the kW, kVAR, and %PF fields and Load Amps and PF activates the Load Amps and %PF fields. Choose the option that best fits the data you have about these circuit elements. 

## Calculated Load Table 
Contains various load calculations based on the values defined below. The phases attributed to the element will be listed as rows in the table and totals will be calculated at the bottom. 

### kW 
The kW load for each available phase of this circuit element. 

### kvar 
The kvar load for each available phase of this circuit element. 

### %PF (Power Factor) 
The power factor assigned to this circuit element based on the assigned calculated load. Power Factor is calculated if kvar is entered and kvar is calculated if Power Factor is entered. 

### Cons (Consumers) 
The number of consumers connected to each available phase of this circuit element. 

### Load Amps 
The calculated load amps on each available phase of this circuit element. If changed, kW and kvar will be updated accordingly. %PF will be held constant. 

### Line Amps 
The calculated line amps on each available phase of this circuit element. This current is calculated using load connected to this circuit element only and does not include any downline load. This field is calculated only and cannot be edited. 

## Load Mix 
The following defines the field values under the Load Mix section: 

### % kVA 
The percentage of load on this circuit element that is assumed to be constant kVA in its voltage to current relationship. This value is for display only and is determined by the Load Mix code for this circuit element. 

### % Imp 
The percentage of load on this circuit element that is assumed to be constant impedance in its voltage to current relationship. This value is for display only and is determined by the Load Mix code for this circuit element. 

### % Amp 
The percentage of load on this circuit element that is assumed to be constant current in its voltage to current relationship. This value is for display only and is determined by the Load Mix code for this circuit element. 

### % P 
The values under this column designate the kW values for each field. 

### % Q 
The values under this column designate the kVAr values for each field. 

## Base Volts 
The nominal voltage (or base voltage) used in kVA to amps and amps to kVA calculations. If this value is changed, Load Amps and Line Amps will be updated accordingly. This value is line-to-ground if the line is connected Wye and is line-to-line if the line is connected Delta. 

## Amps Calculated at (Volts) 
The actual voltage used in kVA to amps and amps to kVA calculations. If this value is changed, Load Amps and Line Amps will be updated accordingly. 

## Amps Calculated at (Per Unit) 
The actual voltage (per unit) used in kVA to amps and amps to kVA calculations. If this value is changed, Load Amps and Line Amps will be updated accordingly.
capacitor:
## Capacitor Bank is Connected 
Defines the capacitor bank as Series or Shunt. 

## Volt Rating of Capacitor Units 
Gives the voltage rating of the capacitor units. If set to "0," the capacitor rating will be assumed to be the same as the nominal. (Tip: Series capacitors are usually rated significantly less than the system nominal voltage.)

## Shunt Capacitor Connection 
Defines the capacitor bank connection as Wye, Delta, or as the same connection as the element's parent. 

## Capacitor Kvar Rating 
Allows you to manually alter kvar values: 

## All Phases the Same 
Forces the same capacitor kvar on all phases. If not checked, a value for each phase must be entered and a different kvar for each phase may be entered. If checked, a value for only the first existing phase is required. This value will then be assigned to all other existing phases. 

## kvar (A/B/C) 
Gives the total capacitor bank and total phase rating in kvar. Each phase can be independently controlled if All Phases the Same is not checked. The total phase kvar is calculated as the Capacitor Unit Size times Units in Parallel. 

## Capacitor Output Is 
Defines the calculated kvar and current output of the capacitor bank when the voltage is as defined by the When Voltage is field. These fields are for information only and may not be edited by the user. Changing the size of the capacitor bank the voltage rating or When Voltage Is will cause these fields to be recalculated. 

## When Voltage Is 
Allows you to select the voltage at which Capacitor Output Is is calculated. Changing any of these fields will cause an appropriate change in the other voltage fields as well as the appropriate change in Capacitor Output fields.
conductor_data:
## All Phases the Same 
Places one conductor on all available phases. Use the Phase A (if it exists) to select the conductor. 

If the A-Phase does not exist, then you can use the first available phase on the circuit element. 

If the checkbox is not selected, you will be required to enter a conductor for each available phase. This allows you to model different conductors on each phase. 

## Per-phase Conductors 
Controls how many conductors are used on each phase of this line. Lines may have 1, 2, or 3 conductors per phase. 

## Neutral 
The neutral conductor. If this field is blank, the conductor used for the neutral will be defined by the Preferred Neutral Conductor of the conductor on the first existing phase. 

## Number of Neutrals 
Controls how many neutral conductors are used on this line. If no neutral is desired, set this value to “0”. Overhead lines may have 0, 1, or 2 neutrals. 

## Construction 
Defines the spacing used to calculate impedance for overhead and underground circuit elements. 

If the Construction field is left blank, the entry for Preferences|System|Modeling|System Default Construction Type will be used. 

As a shortcut, you can define the System Default Construction Type to be the most commonly used overhead and underground construction standards for your system. Then, leave Construction fields blank on all line elements that use this spacing default. This will reduce the amount of required data input. 

## Parallel With 
The program will allow you to put one line on top of another. However, if the selected line is sharing poles with another line, you can use this text box to identify that other line by name. The analysis algorithm will change slightly, based on the lines' proximity to one another. 

## Graphical Length 
The length in display or model units of the line elements. The units will correspond to real world units if your model was natively created in real world units. These are the native coordinates of your model without any conversion applied. 

## Impedance Length 
The impedance length of the circuit element in survey feet, which is based on actual length that varies with sag tables and vertical change between poles. The impedance of the line element will be based upon this length, unless the Conductor is defined as a Zsm type conductor with the Units field set to “Total”.
consumer_data:
## Active Consumer 
Identifies the consumer element as an active meter. 

## Has Generation 
Determines whether to enable the consumer generation data tab. 

## Consumer Type 
Identifies the consumer as being Residential, Small Commercial, Large Commercial, Large Power, Motor Load, Irrigation, Oil and Gas, Traffic Lights, Security and Street Lights, Flat Rate Load, Primary, Primary 120V, or Test 120V. 

## CIS Link 
The CIS Link is the Location ID in the CIS system. This is used for integrations.

## Automated Meter Reading Data 
Contains information obtained through an interface with an AMR system. 

## Meter Number 
The meter number of the currently selected consumer. 

## AMR Vendor 
The AMR vendor for the currently selected consumer's meter. Not editable.

## AMR Device Type 
The AMR device type for the currently selected consumer's meter. Not editable.

## kW Read Time 
The exact time of the reading of the meter. Not editable.

## Momentary interruptions 
Lists the number of momentary interruptions, like power surges or one-second outages, that the meter has recorded. Not editable.

## Sustained outages 
Lists the number of sustained outages that the meter has recorded. Not editable.

## Signal strength 
The signal strength of the AMR. Not editable.

## Meter Multiplier 
The watt-hour billing multiplier of the meter. Not editable.
consumer_generation:
Consumer generation allows behind-the-meter generation to be defined separately from consumer load. This is used by analysis algorithms to calculate current flow for consumers that also provide power to the grid. 

## Generated kVA Table 
Contains various power inputs based on the values defined below. The phases attributed to the element will be listed as rows in the table and totals will be calculated at the bottom. 

## kW 
The kW generated for each available phase of this circuit element. 

## kvar 
The kvar generated for each available phase of this circuit element. 

## %PF (Power Factor) 
The power factor assigned to this circuit element based on the assigned generated kVA. Power Factor is calculated if kvar is entered and kvar is calculated if Power Factor is entered. 

## Balance Phases Button 
When clicked, this will distribute the kVA defined in the totals row of the Generated kVA Table evenly among the active phases of the circuit element.
device_data:
## Device Code 
Provides a way to set the overcurrent device equipment for use on this circuit element. This code defines the device characteristics and its coordination with other devices. Type in the name of existing equipment or click the button to display the Equipment Editor for Devices, and select the desired device code from the list or create a new device. 

*Tip: The device code is what gives an overcurrent device its type. For example, if you choose fuse as the device code, any element that uses that equipment will be displayed as a fuse and will behave as a fuse during circuit analysis.* 

## Device Status 
Defines the overcurrent device to be Closed or Open. Each phase may be set independently if All Phases the Same is not selected. 

## Feeder Checkbox 
Controls whether or not it is a feeder level device. Formerly, this functionality was located in the Node element. 

## Number 
A number for the selected feeder. 

## Color 
The color that will be used for this feeder in Color By Feeder mode. 

## Alias 
An alternate name for this device to be used for identifying a feeder in the work environment. If your overcurrent device is named OCD1, but its feeder alias is FDR3, FDR3 will appear as this element's name in the work environment. If there is no alias, the element's real name will be used. 

## Control Point 
Designates the selected element as a Load Allocation Control Point. 

## Edit Data Button 
Opens the Load Allocation Control Point Editor. This button is only enabled if Control Point is checked. 

## If Fuse Protecting Reclosing Device 
The method that should be used to coordinate this fuse device with an upline recloser. This field has no effect if there is no fuse device associated with this element. This setting may also be ignored depending on the Coordination Analysis settings. (See the coordination test settings section for details.)
external_tables:
Tip: Your model must be connected to External Tables, and the selected element's type must have external tables, for the “External” tab to show. 

The “External” tab enables you to store and keep track of any extra data that the engineering model does not store. Element types can be connected to many external tables, and you can use the drop-down at the top of the tab to switch between them.
fault_model: This tab enables you to assign the equipment for each stage of a generator start-up.
files:
This Circuit Element Editor tab allows editing and viewing files attached to the selected circuit element. You can have up to 10 files attached to a circuit element with file size limited to 5mb per file. As long as File Service is running on the server, any files attached to the selected circuit element will automatically sync to all other linked local models on the network. 

The “Files” tab in the Circuit Element Editor 

Click the **Add** button to attach a file to the selected circuit element. 

Click the **Remove** button to remove the currently selected file from the selected circuit element. 

Click the **Open** button to launch the default application associated with this file type. 

Click the **>** button to navigate to the next file. 

Click the **<** button to navigate to the previous file.
generators:
## Generator Model 
Gives you “Negative Load” or “Swing kvar” source options for defining your generator model. 

## Total Generator kVA 
The desired total kW and kvar output for the generator. If kvar is set, then PF is calculated. If PF is set, then kvar is calculated. The specified kW will be modeled as a negative load or as a source of kW to the circuit. The kvar will be modeled negative to its specified sign. A positive PF will be seen as a source of kvar to the circuit. A negative PF will be seen as a kvar load to the circuit. Tip: These fields are only available if the Generator Model is Negative Load.

## Generator is to hold 
The magnitude of voltage, in per unit, that the generator is to maintain. Tip: This field is only available if the Generator Model is Swing kvar.

## Control Element 
The element that the generator will hold the per unit voltage for. Tip: This field is only available if the Generator Model is Swing kvar.

## Output is set at 
The kW output of the generator. This will be the fixed kW injected into the circuit by the generator. Tip: This field is only available if the Generator Model is Swing kvar.

## Maximum leading output 
The maximum leading (positive) kvar output of the generator. The algorithm will not limit the kvar at this level, but will flag the generator graphically and on printouts if it exceeds this limit. Tip: This field is only available if the Generator Model is Swing kvar.

## Maximum lagging output 
The maximum lagging (negative) kvar output of the generator. The algorithm will not limit the kvar at this level, but will flag the generator graphically and on printouts if it exceeds this limit. Tip: This field is only available if the Generator Model is Swing kvar.

## Allow Swing Generator to Exceed kVAR Limits 
If true, the results of an analysis run may exceed the setpoint values in order to force the “Voltage to Hold” value to be met. Tip: This field is only available if the Generator Model is Swing kvar.

## Connected 
Gives you Wye or Delta connection options.
impedance:
The “Impedance” tab will show the three-phase impedance matrix (Zabc matrix) for a particular element, or the accumulated impedance from the source to the element. 

Because the impedance matrix shows the impedance values that were calculated during the most recent voltage drop analysis, you will need to run a voltage drop in order for the results to be valid. 

The “Impedance” tab of the Circuit Element Editor 

You can now copy the values directly from the tables on this tab.
load_mix:
## Load Mix Equipment Button 
Lets you choose load mix equipment from the equipment database. A load mix is used to define the mix between constant kVA, constant impedance, and constant current load models. It is also used to define the load as delta-connected or wye-connected. If this text box is left blank, the system default is used. 

## Load Zone Equipment Button 
Places the selected element in a load zone. Load zones are used to define load growth by region. 

## Load Location 
Allows you to choose whether the load on an element is modeled at its source end, its load end, or distributed uniformly over the length of the element. Obviously, this makes the most sense with line elements. 

## Load Is 
Allows you to choose whether the load on the element is classified as General and is used by Contingency Analysis when it is deciding where to drop load. 

## Billing 
Allows you to give this element a numeric index for interfacing with other systems.
locked_rotor: Use this tab to assign values to the motors in your circuit model based on the specifications provided by the manufacturer.
motor_data:
## Motor Mode 
A drop-down that contains three fields you can use to specialize a motor's information: Horse Power, Fixed kW, and Fixed Slip. All other settings on this tab will be made active or inactive based on the mode selection. 

## Total Motor HP 
The rated motor horse power. 

## % Utilization 
The percentage of rated horse power actually generated by the motor. Allowed values range from 0% to 1000% (0 to 10 times rated output). 

## %PF at Full Load 
The percent power factor of the motor at full load and full speed operating conditions. 

## % Eff. at Full Load 
The percent efficiency of the motor at full load and full speed operating conditions. 

## Rated LG Volts 
The rated line-to-ground voltage of the motor. Enter the LG and the LL will be calculated. This will also be available when the Advanced Model option is selected. 

## Rated LL Volts 
The rated line-to-line voltage of the motor. Enter the LL and the LG will be calculated. This will also be available when the Advanced Model option is selected. 

## Drop Out if % Voltage < 
The voltage level in percent of rated voltage at which the motors holding coil will drop out. This entry will be used by the analysis Motor Analysis application to flag motors that are caused to drop out by the starting of other motors on the circuit. 

## Load in kW 
The calculated motor kW load for the specified motor horse power and efficiency. This data field is for information only and cannot be modified, unless the Advanced Model option is selected. 

Motor kW = horse power * 74.6 / percent efficiency 

## Load in kvar 
The calculated motor kvar load for the specified motor horse power efficiency and power factor. This data field is for information only and cannot be modified. 

Motor kvar = Motor kW * tan(acos(percent power factor /100) 

## Percent Slip 
The difference between a motor's synchronous speed and its speed at full load. It measures the speed performance of an induction motor. 

## Motor Status 
The status of the selected motor. This will be the status of the motor during locked rotor calculations. 

## Motor Conductor 
Becomes active if the Advanced Model option is selected. Select the motor's conductor equipment by pressing the Equipment button. 

### Notes
If no motors are set to Locked Rotor and Soft Start, the results will be the same as for pre-locked rotor calculations.
nodes:
## Circuit Level 
Defines how this node will be used for modeling. However, the values in this field are not currently used in any analysis. Setting the circuit level to "None" is always safe. 

## Node is Mandatory 
Used by Circuit Reducer to determine if this is a mandatory node. If Mandatory, then this element is not eliminated during the Circuit Reduction process. 

## Control Point 
Designates the selected node as a Load Allocation Control Point. 

## Edit Data Button 
Opens the Load Allocation Control Point Editor. This button is only enabled if Control Point is checked. 

## Node is Multi-Parent 
Defines the node as having multiple parents. This allows single-phase and two-phase line elements to be connected so that a three-phase segment can be formed. Multiparent nodes should rarely be used.
polygon: This tab lists all of the polygons to which the currently selected element is connected. The information listed under each shape file in this tab is based on the fields imported with each shape file.
profiles:
A Voltage Profile is a chart that shows the voltages of each circuit element along a path to the source. The names of the elements in the path are shown across the bottom of the chart and their corresponding voltages are shown to the left of the chart. Since the profile shows the resulting voltages from the most recent voltage drop analysis, you will need to run a Voltage Drop in order for the results to be valid. 

## Property to Profile Drop-Down 
Contains the options for displaying either a Voltage Profile or a Current Profile on the bottom part of the tab. 

## Values in Terms of 
Contains three radio buttons, which control the units on the Y axis of the Voltage or Current Profile. 

## Edit Graph Button 
Opens a dialog for customizing the profile. This button is at the top left corner of the profile section.

## Popout Button 
Opens a floating copy of the profile graph. This floating copy will not change if you open a different element in the circuit element editor, or if you run an analysis that changes the results in the profile. This allows you to compare the profile of an element at some point in time with the profiles of other elements. 

*This button is at the top right corner of the profile section.* 

## Voltage or Current Profile 
A chart that shows the voltages, or currents, respectively, of each circuit element along a path to the source. The names of the elements in the path are shown across the bottom of the chart and their corresponding values are shown to the left of the chart. 

Since a Voltage Profile shows the resulting voltages from the most recent voltage drop analysis, you will need to run a voltage drop in order for the results to be valid.
regulator_data:
## Control Element 
The regulator "Voltage Setting" will apply to the Control Element. Normally this would be the regulator itself, but by setting to some other element, control based on remote voltage metering may be used. 

## Winding 
Contains different regulator winding settings. By default, regulators are modeled as Y-Y. 

## Phasing 
The following are options under the Phasing drop-down menu: 

## 1-phase units with all phases the same 
The option that should be selected for a single-phase regulator unit on a single-phase circuit, or for single-phase regulator units banked together on two-and three-phase circuits where the settings are not different. A bank of single-phase regulator units will be modeled where all units will have the same settings and size definitions. 

## 1-phase units with different settings 
The option that should be selected for single-phase regulator units banked together on two and three phase circuits where the settings are different. This option is available for phase configurations with more than one phase. For phase configurations of two or three phases, a bank of single-phase regulator units (one unit on each phase) will be modeled. All units will have individual settings and size definitions. 

## 3-phase controlled by phase 
Only an option for 3-phase regulators. Choose the controlling phase of this regulator. 

If the number of regulator units is less than the number of phases, such as a three-phase circuit with one single-phase regulator unit: 

1. Set phase to the phase configuration appropriate for the circuit location.

2. Select 1-Phase Units with different settings.

3. Select (may need to create) a Regulator Size Definition with Boost % and Buck % set to 0.0 for each phase without a regulator. 

## Regulator Settings in Terms of... 
Sets the Regulator settings in terms of Percent, Per Unit or Volts. These options will change the Regulator settings at the bottom of the tab. 

## Base Voltage 
The base voltage for regulator settings, if Volts is selected above. 

For example, if “120” is entered, regulator settings will be displayed on a 120 volt base and should be entered in terms of a 120 volt base. 

## Regulator Size Definition 
Provides a way to select (or create) the definition of regulator amp rating, primary CT rating, percent boost, percent buck, step size, and bandwidth. 

To create or select a regulator size definition, type in a valid description or click the button to open the equipment editor, and then select the desired regulator definition. 

## Voltage Level 
The output voltage of the regulator, if line drop compensation is not used. If line drop compensation (LD CompR and LD CompX) is used, the output voltage is the adjustable target voltage or the voltage at zero amps. 

## LD CompR 
The line drop compensation resistance setting. If you are not going to use line drop compensation, set it to zero. This value is entered as a voltage. 

## LD CompX 
The line drop compensation reactance setting. If you are not going to use line drop compensation, set it to"0." This value is entered as a voltage. 

## First House High 
Specifies the high voltage limiting or first house protector setting. Within its specified boost-buck range, the regulator will not allow a boost condition that results in the voltage being higher than this value if it is set. If you are not going to use the first house protector, set it to "0." 

## First House Low 
Specifies the low voltage limiting or first house protector setting. Within its specified boost-buck range, the regulator will not allow a buck condition that results in the voltage being lower than this setting. Set it to "0" if no First House Protector is used. 

## Bypass 
Tells the program to skip this particular regulator on checked phases. If you change the Phasing to "3ph controlled by phase", checking the Bypass checkbox for the control phase will force the other phases to be bypassed as well.
reliability:
This tab provides two text boxes for you to enter reliability data for the currently active element, such as how long it takes to repair the element. 

The general “Reliability” tab in the Circuit Element Editor 

The fields that appear on this tab will differ depending on what sort of element is selected. All elements have the two fields displayed in this “Reliability” tab and some elements, like overhead and underground lines, consumers, generators, motors and nodes will have only these two fields. 

Others require a few more. For example, switches often need to be closed, opened, or bypassed when repairs are being made to a circuit, so those time fields are added to a device's “Reliability” tab. 

## Failure Rate 
Annual number of failures expected on an element or category of element. The failure rate for equipment is expressed in failures per year for each device. So if an element or category of elements is expected to fail once every ten years, its failure rate is 0.10. The failure rate for lines, as a category, is expressed in failures per mile per year. For a given line element, the failure rate is expressed in failures per year. 

## Repair Time 
The average time required to repair a failure on element or category of elements. This time should be repair time only and not include travel, switching, or time to find problem. 

## Bypass Time 
## The average time required to bypass the element or category of elements. This time should include bypass time only and not include travel, switching, or time to find problem. 

## Close Time 
The average time required to close the element or category of elements. This time should include bypass time only and not include travel, switching, or time to find problem. 

## Open Time 
The average time required to open the element or category of elements. This time should include bypass time only and not include travel, switching, or time to find problem. 

## Coordination Failure Rate 
How often the coordination between two devices will fail. For example, if you expect a fuse to clear a fault before the upline recloser trips out and the fuse remains closed one out of ten times, that fuse would have a 10% coordination failure rate. 

You can also use the Reliability Data Quick Editor or the global editor tools in the Selected Elements Window to simultaneously edit the reliability data for many elements.
soft_start: Use this tab to assign values to the motors in your circuit model based on the specifications provided by the manufacturer.
solar_output:
## Total kWAC 
The total output power for the solar PV system. This can either be entered directly or calculated from the data in the “Array” and “Inverter” tabs. 

## kVAR 
The total kVAR output by the solar PV system. This can either be entered directly or calculated from the data in the “Inverter” tab. 

## Calculate from Array 
If checked, the total output power is calculated from data entered in the “Array” and “Inverter” tabs. Otherwise, the output power can be entered directly. If this is checked, then “Calculate from Inverter” must also be checked.

## Calculate from Inverter 
If checked, the total output kVAR is calculated from data entered in the “Inverter” tab. Otherwise, the output power can be entered directly.

## Total Array kW DC 
The DC output power from the solar array. This is a read-only value taken from the “Array” tab.

## Inverter Rated kVA 
The rated maximum apparent power for the inverter. This is a read-only value taken from the “Inverter” tab.

## Generator Status 
This setting allows output from the solar PV to be turned on or off.

## Connected 
This sets the connection type of the solar PV output to either “Wye” or “Delta”.
solar_array:
This tab provides settings for an array of panels in a solar PV system, including fields for defining DC power and voltage for the array as a whole or calculated from individual panel data and array layout. 

## Manufacturer 
Specifies the manufacturer name of the solar array.

## Model 
Specifies the model name of the solar array.

## Panel Settings Calculator 
Opens a secondary window with settings to define an individual solar panel and the layout of an array. 

## Array kW (PMAX) 
Specifies the maximum DC power output for the solar array. This can be entered directly or calculated from individual panel data.

## Max Power Voltage 
The output DC voltage of the solar array at the maximum power point. This can be entered directly or calculated from individual panel data.

## Max Power Current 
The output DC current of the solar array at the maximum power point. This can be entered directly or calculated from individual panel data.

## Total DC Losses 
The total DC power loss inherent to the solar array. DC losses to be considered here include soiling, shading, snow, module mismatch, wiring, connections, nameplate rating, age, and availability. Do not include temperature-related losses or inverter efficiency. 

## Array Tilt Type 
Defines whether panels in the array can adjust their tilt or azimuth to follow the sun. Options are fixed, 1-axis, and 2-axis.

## Tilt (degrees) 
The tilt angle in degrees of array panels along an East/West axis, where 0 degrees would be parallel with the ground and 90 degrees would be vertical. Optimum sunlight collection angle is nominally equal to the array's latitude.

## Azimuth (degrees) 
The tilt angle in degrees of array panels along a North/South axis. In other words, this represents how inclined the panels are toward the East or the West. 

# Calculate Array Properties From Panels

## Panel Manufacturer 
Specifies the manufacturer name of the solar panel.

## Panel Model 
Specifies the model name of the solar panel.

## Rated Watts 
The maximum power output by one panel.

## Open-circuit Voltage (VOC) 
Specifies the maximum DC voltage output by the panel with no load.

## Max Power Point Voltage (VMPP) 
Specifies the output DC voltage of the panel at the max power point.

## Max Power Point Current (IMPP) 
Specifies the output DC current of the panel at the max power point.

## Short-circuit Current (ISC) 
Specifies the maximum output DC current of the panel when the leads are shorted together.

## Number of Panels in Series (String) 
Specifies the number of panels connected in series for each string of panels in the array.

## Number of Strings in Parallel 
Specifies the number of panel strings connected in parallel.

## Populate Array 
When clicked, data from this window is used to update the Array kW, Max Power Voltage, and Max Power Current fields on the “Solar Array” tab.
solar_fault:
## Full Load Amps at Rated Volts 
This value is taken from the “Solar Inverter” tab. It is shown here to assist in visualizing the results of fault analysis as related to nominal operating current. 

## Rated AC Volts 
This value is taken from the “Solar Inverter” tab. It is shown here to assist in visualizing the results of fault analysis as related to nominal operating voltage. 

## Fault Current Multiplier 
The multiplier used for the line-to-ground current found from a lookup table based on accumulated X/R at the fault point. Multiply this by the line-to-ground fault current to find the asymmetric line-to-ground fault.

## Fault Current X/R 
The X/R ratio at the fault point used to find the multiplier to calculate the line-to-ground asymmetrical fault value.

## LLL Fault 
The maximum 3-phase fault current. This is a complex value displayed as a magnitude and a phase angle in degrees.

## LL Fault 
The maximum 3-phase fault current. This is a complex value displayed as a magnitude and a phase angle in degrees.
solar_inverter:
## Operating Mode 
Determines how the inverter adjusts to available power and phase conditions. Currently, only “Constant PQ” is available. 

## Manufacturer 
Specifies the manufacturer name of the solar inverter.

## Model 
Specifies the model name of the solar inverter.

## Phase 
Specifies whether the inverter is connected as a single-phase or three-phase device.

## Rated kVA 
The rated output apparent power of the inverter, in kVA.

## Rated AC Volts 
The rated output AC voltage of the inverter.

## Full Load AC Amps 
The rated ouptut AC current of the inverter. 

## Rated DC Watts 
The rated input power capacity of the inverter, in watts.

## Rated DC Volts 
The rated input DC voltage of the inverter.

## Full Load DC Amps 
The rated input DC current capacity of the inverter. 

## DC-AC Efficiency 
The expected ratio of output AC power to input DC power, expressed as a percentage. 

## Operating PF 
The expected ratio of output real power to apparent power, expressed as a percentage.
source_data:
## Base Out Voltage 
The default voltage for all sources. This can be changed on the “Modeling” tab of the System Preferences dialog. 

## Impedance Code Min 
The impedance code used to calculate maximum fault values. It provides a way to define the impedance for the source, which represents the equivalent impedance between the source and the infinite supply bus. 

## Impedance Code Max 
The impedance code used to calculate minimum fault values. 

To enter the impedance code for an element, type in a valid description or click the button to open the Equipment Editor for Zsm Conductor. Then, select the desired impedance code from the list or create the desired impedance definition. 

## Sub Number 
A substation number for the source. 

## Bus Voltage 
The initial voltage level at the source. If the base voltage is “120” and regulation is set to “105%” of the nominal primary line-to-ground, the bus volts would be set to “126”. 

126 = 1.05 * 120 

If the nominal primary line-to-ground voltage is 7200 volts, the actual source primary voltage would then be set to 7560 volts. 

7560 = 7200 * 126 / 120 

## Angle 
The angle (in degrees) for the source voltage relative to the current. 

## OH Ground Ohms 
The impedance, in ohms, used to calculate the minimum line-to-ground fault on overhead lines. 

## UG Ground Ohms 
The impedance, in ohms, to be used to calculate the minimum line-to-ground fault on underground lines. 

## Base L-G 
Specifies the base line-to-ground output voltage of the source. Enter the L-G and the L-L will be calculated. This value has a valid range from 0.01 to 999999.99. 

## Base L-L 
Specifies the base line-to-line output voltage of the source. Enter the L-L and L-G will be calculated. This value has a valid range from 0.01 to 999999.99. 

Base voltage is the primary voltage required on the primary terminals of a no-taps distribution transformer to produce 120 line-to-ground volts on the secondary terminals assuming a 120/240 volt distribution transformer. 

For example, the base voltage of a system using 7200/120 transformers would be 7200 volts. 

## Feeder Color 
The color that the source and all circuits directly downline will appear in whenever the program is in Color by Feeder mode. Note: If a device defined as a feeder bay sits between this source and the rest of the circuit, the circuit will not be colored. You must change the color of the feeder bay to get the rest of the circuit to change color.

## Control Point 
This box must be selected if this source is to be used as a Load Allocation Control Point. 

## Edit Data Button 
Opens the Load Allocation Control Point dialog box. 

## Connection 
Specifies the source connection as Wye or Delta. Delta should be selected only for systems with no ground return path. 

## Regulation 
Specifies the source as regulated or unregulated. 

If Yes is selected, the source is modeled as regulated, and the source voltage will be held at the specified Bus Voltage value. 

If No is selected, the source is modeled as unregulated, and the source voltage will be the specified Bus Voltage less the drop across the impedance specified by the Impedance Code Min.
switch_data:
## Switch Id 
An alphanumeric identifier for the switch and its partner. 

## Switch Status 
Allows a switch to be selected as Open, Closed, or Looped. 

A looped switch is a closed switch that creates a loop in the system. Because distribution systems are generally radial systems, your model should not contain many looped switches. 

If your model does contain looped switches, you can set up some analysis modes to ignore them. Otherwise, the program will perform a looped analysis on your system instead of the standard radial analysis. 

## Switch Partner 
The name of the other side of the currently selected switch. Click the Go To button to open the other side of the switch in the Editor.
switch_options: This tab contains options and design specifications for the switches in your model.
transformer_data:
## Winding Connections 
Defines the winding connection configuration of the transformer. Your choice here will determine what other fields need to be filled in. The available winding connection options are defined in the Winding Connections Table. 

| Winding Connections Table ||
| --- | --- |
| Connections | Notes |  
| Y-Y | Grd Grounded Wye-Wye. |  
| Y-Y | ImpGrd Wye-Wye grounded through specified grounding impedances. |  
| Y-Y | 3PhCore Three phase with 3-legged core grounded Wye-Wye. |  
| Y-D | Grd Grounded Wye-Delta. |  
| Y-D | one One line to line connected transformer. |  
| Y-D | open Grounded Wye-Delta with two transformers supplying three phase service. |  
| Y-D | unGrd Ungrounded Wye-Delta. |  
| D-Y | Grd Delta-Grounded Wye. |  
| D-Y | one One line to ground or line to line connected transformer. |  
| D-Y | open Two line to line connected transformers supplying two phase service. |  
| D-D | Delta-Delta. |  
| D-D | one One line to line connected transformer. |  
| D-D | open Delta-Delta with two transformers supplying three phase service. |  
| Y-Y-D | Grd Grounded Wye — grounded Wye — Delta (tertiary) three winding transformer. |  

## Impedance Definition 
Defines the impedance characteristics and kVA size of each transformer. Enter a transformer definition by typing in a valid description or clicking the button to open the equipment editor. Select the desired transformer definition from the list or create a new definition. 

Selecting the Center Tap checkbox next to in impedance definition designates that phase as the master center tap phase downline. The line connect of all elements downline will be center tap. When you are using a transformer with Y-D open, Y-D one, or Y-D ungrounded windings, you will be given the option to set a phase as Center Tap. Center Tap transformers will display a Center Tap L-G and L-L voltage. They will also set the line connect downline to Center Tap (rather than Wye or Delta). You can also set an element's load to be connected Center Tap: Load Mixes can now be set to include Center Tap load. Elements with a Center Tap load mix will be understood to have Center Tap load. In load dialogs, the two phases off of a Center Tap transformer will be referred to as A1 and A2, if the incoming phasing is AB, B1 and B2, if the incoming phasing is BC, and C1 and C2, if the incoming phasing is AC. When Center Tap Loaded elements are rephased, their conductors and load are always rotated. 

## Primary Rated Voltage 
The transformer namplate-rated voltage for primary winding at the neutral tap. 

## Tap At 
(Primary Tap Voltage / Primary Rated Voltage) * 100.0. Tap At is in percent. 

## Primary Tap Voltage 
Primary Rated Voltage * (Tap At / 100.0). 

## Secondary Rated Voltage 
The transformer namplate-rated voltage for the secondary winding. 

If the transformer has a load tap changer, Secondary Rated Voltage should be set to the neutral tap voltage and the tap changer should be modeled using a regulator in series with the transformer. 

## Secondary System Base 
The voltage used as Base Voltage for per-unit calculations on the system downline from the transformer. 

## Rated Input Voltage 
The nominal voltage for all the system upline from the transformer. 

## Rated Output Voltage 
The nominal voltage for all the system downline from the transformer. The Input Voltage then sets the transformation ratio of the transformer. 

## Nominal of Output System 
The nominal voltage of the system connected to the transformer. 

Enter the nominal L-G or L-L voltage of the system downline from the transformer. The Nominal of Output System is the voltage required on the secondary terminals of a no taps distribution transformer to produce 120 line to ground volts using a 7200/120 volt distribution transformer. 

For example, the nominal output voltage of a system using 7200/120 transformers would be 120 volts. 

# Notes
Definition of transformer winding connections and grounding are based upon the Electrical Transmission and Distribution Reference Book, Table 7.
